units.translation: Accusative as if from a nominative ἄμαλς [a ship], which no one has used. Hesychius: ἄμαλα [the ship]: the ship, from ἀμᾶν [to reap] τὴν ἅλα [the sea]. Aeschylus in the satyric Proteus (fr. 212). Corruptly in Etym. M. p. 75.22: ἀμάδα [the ship] in Aeschylus. Hermann restored ἐπ᾽ ἅμαλα [upon the ships] for the corrupt ἐπαμίδα [a kind of cake] in Suppl. 842, 847.
ἄμαλα [the ship]: the ship, from ἀμᾶν [to reap] τὴν ἅλα [the sea].

Excellent is the emendation of Henri Weil for γάμῳ δαπτομέναν [being torn in marriage], which M has with the letters το written by a somewhat later hand in an erasure of three letters, which were undoubtedly ανω, i.e. δαπανωμένην [being consumed], which is preserved in several copies, written partly thus, partly δαπανομένην [being consumed]. The word γάμῳ [in marriage] is not corrupted from μέγα [great], as Schütz persuaded many, but has a far different origin. For after in a book much older than the Medicean codex ἈΜΑΛΑΠΤΟΜΕΝAN [being utterly destroyed] had been corrupted into ἈΜΑΔΑΠΤΟΜΕΝΑΝ [being torn], to AMA, which seemed to be ἅμα [together with], the dative γάμῳ [in marriage] was added, with ἅμα [together with] noted in the margin, and δαπτομέναν [being torn] explained by δαπανωμένην [being consumed]. Hence was produced what is now read in M, with a scholium added in the margin, which was perhaps composed by a corrector, like many others: γάμψ: ἅμα τῷ γάμῳ· λείπει γὰρ τὸ ἅμα [marriage: together with the marriage; for 'together with' is missing]. Thomas Magister supplied ἐν [in], in whose scholium among other things these are read: εἰσορῶσα αὐτὴν δαπτομένην καὶ δαμαζομένην ἐν τῷ γάμῳ τοῦ Διός [seeing her being torn and subdued in the marriage of Zeus], and in the interlinear gloss: τὴν παρθενίαν δηλοῖ ἀφανιζομένην [it indicates her virginity being destroyed]. An older Byzantine scholiast: τῷ γάμῳ τῷ τοῦ Διὸς δαπτομένην καὶ δακνομένην [being torn and bitten by the marriage of Zeus]. In the Wittenberg copy the gloss is κινδυνεύουσαν [being in danger].
